free_tier.stated: Free: 1 GB cloud storage, 1 download slot, download speed 'Not guaranteed', 'Unsecured Only HTTP', 'Without antivirus control', online streaming on all devices, no extra features.
free_tier.notes: the free plan is storage-metered; a 20 GiB torrent cannot fit in 1 GB

per_object_cap.stated: No per-torrent cap is published. The free plan's cap is the 1 GB storage total.
per_object_cap.notes: third-party reviews report a one-torrent-per-day limit on free accounts; that number is not on the vendor's pricing page

retention.stated: Not stated on the pricing or features pages. The terms say that when a user's space expires 'the Company will delete all data uploaded by the User onto the Server'.
retention.notes: files appear to persist while the plan is active; no inactivity clock is published

egress.terms: Paid plans list 'Unlimited Download speed'; free is 'Not guaranteed' and served over plain HTTP. No byte allowance is published on any plan.

interface_detail: HTTPS download links per file from the web UI; the free plan is explicitly HTTP-only. No public API is documented on the pages read.
tooling: browser; FTP and RSS are paid-plan features ('RSS downloader' is listed from the Small plan up). No SDK.
chaining: one of the few torrent-to-cloud services that advertises torrent and magnet only, so it drops into a stack as a pure fetch hop; 75 GB for $5 is the cheapest per-GB paid tier read after TorBox.

limits.value: 1 GB stored on free; 75 GB on Small, 250 GB on Standard, 1 TB on Big
1 download slot on free; 5 on Small, 20 on Standard, 30 on Big
1 GB of cloud storage on the free plan; 75 GB Small, 250 GB Standard, 1 TB Big

limits_note: third-party reviews (torrentcompare 2019, rapidseedbox 2023) put the free plan at one torrent per day; the vendor's own help-centre page 'How much can I download per month?' is a JavaScript shell and returned no text through the reader.
binding_note: The 1 GB storage total rejects a 20 GiB torrent before any slot or per-day limit applies.

identity_cost.detail: free account signup. The terms describe paid plans paid by card, PayPal or Bitcoin; the free plan needs no payment method.

reliability_note: free-tier downloads are HTTP-only and un-antivirused, unlike the paid tiers; the site has been running since at least 2016 and its help centre is now partly JavaScript-only.
confidence_note: the four plans and their limits were read from the vendor's pricelist. The free per-day torrent count is reported, not documented.

price_per_tb_month: USD 5 for 75 GB; USD 15 for 1 TB
notes: The free tier is the smallest of the western torrent-to-cloud services: 1 GB cannot hold a single episode. The paid entry, 75 GB for $5, is the second cheapest per byte after TorBox Essential, but the free plan's per-day limit means the service is bought for storage, not queue depth. The ladder's own row says 'storage cap' and then adds the 1 GB into a byte-committed monthly subtotal. It is the one row in that subtotal that does not multiply. The number is defensible as a conservative floor, and it is wrong as a monthly ceiling in both directions: a 2 GB torrent is refused outright, and a 1 GB file can be downloaded more than once. Recording it as 1 GB/month is a choice, and it should be labelled as a floor rather than a counter.
